text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 26 in history:
1757 - The French defeated the English at the battle of Hastenbeck in the Seven Years War.
1788 - New York State ratified the new constitution and became the 11th state of the Union.
1847 - Liberia became the first independent republic in Africa.
1856 - George Bernard Shaw, playwright, journalist and critic, born in Dublin. Major works include "Caesar and Cleopatra", "Man and Superman", "Major Barbara" and "Saint Joan".
1858 - Lionel Rothschild became the first Jewish member to take his seat in the British House of Commons.
1863 - Samuel Houston died. U.S. soldier and statesman, governor of Tennessee and president of the republic of Texas.
1874 - U.S. conductor Serge Koussevitsky born in Russia. He was conductor of the Boston Symphony Orchestra and founder of the Tanglewood Music Festival.
1875 - Carl Gustav Jung, Swiss psychiatrist, born. Founder of "analytical psychology", he introduced the concepts of introvert and extrovert personalities.
1882 - Wagner's opera "Parsifal" was first performed, at Bayreuth, western Germany.
1894 - Aldous Leonard Huxley, British novelist and essayist, born. He was best known for his novel "Brave New World", warning of the dangers of a scientific age.
1908 - The Federal Bureau of Investigation was created and referred to as Office of the Chief Examiner. It became the FBI in 1935.

1908 - Salvador Allende Gossens born in Chile. Physician and politician, he became Chile's first Marxist president in 1970. He was overthrown and died in a coup by General Augusto Pinochet on September 11, 1973.
1922 - Blake Edwards, U.S. film director best known for his "Pink Panther" films, born.
1928 - Stanley Kubrick, U.S. film director, born. His best known films include the science fiction work "2001 - A Space Odyssey", "Dr Strangelove" and "A Clockwork Orange".
1941 - President Franklin Roosevelt appointed General Douglas MacArthur as Commander of U.S Forces in the Far East.
1941 - Roosevelt froze all Japanese assets in the U.S., virtually halting Japanese-American trade.
1943 - Mick Jagger, lead singer and founder member of the Rolling Stones rock group, born.
1952 - King Farouk of Egypt abdicated and was ordered to leave the country, three days after a coup led by General Neguib.
1952 - Eva Peron, the celebrated first lady of Argentina during the populist government of Juan Peron, died of cancer at age 33.
1953 - Fidel Castro led a failed assault on the Moncada military barracks near Santiago de Cuba in the fight against dictator Fulgencio Batista.
1956 - Under President Nasser, Egypt nationalised the Suez Canal.
1965 - The Maldive Islands in the Indian Ocean became independent, having been a British protectorate since 1887.
1986 - Averell Harriman died. U.S. politician and diplomat, he was a major influence on presidents Roosevelt, Truman and Kennedy. In 1965 President Johnson made him ambassador at large.
1993 - A draft of South Africa's first post-apartheid constitution was presented to democracy negotiators.
